analysis: Reviewed the two head-text excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines 2005-3778). The change updates synthetic golden test vectors. The json_object vector gains template_input.additional_context {enable_thinking:false} (head lines 3020-3022), plus new prompt_token_count 767, new block chain hashes (a third 768-token boundary is dropped), and different token_ids. All content is public synthetic text ("Public synthetic cache-parity input", "Follow instructions.") with no secrets, credentials, keys, attestation material or consumer data. The fixture is test data only and changes no runtime authorization, App Attest, encryption, routing or key handling, so it does not touch TB-011, TB-002, A-016 or the other threats. The most relevant indirect surface is the prefix-cache threat T-041: chain_hash block boundaries feed cache keys, so the changed boundary count (2 blocks at 256/512 for 767 tokens, last complete block 512) is consistent with block-aligned hashing. Whether the production Swift or Go code actually produces these values (enable_thinking:false injection, token IDs, chain hashes) cannot be verified here because the implementing source and the full patch were not supplied; the patch excerpt is truncated. Unverified contract for the next pass: confirm that the code change adding additional_context/enable_thinking for json_object keeps the cache key and prompt_contract_id domain separation. Here prompt_contract_id is unchanged (8171fec3...) even though the rendered prompt and tokens changed, so confirm the contract ID is not meant to cover template-affecting changes. That is a correctness and cache-parity question, not a demonstrated vulnerability. No findings.
